image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, kneeling at dusk in a backyard and pushing loose dark earth back into a hole with both hands

storyboard.claim: The house makes Julia bury the truth for love and money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia refilling the hole she was meant to dig up
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the moral trap: she has chosen the estate's safety over the bones.
storyboard.addedInformation: She is the one covering the grave again, not a ghost.

image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house, not a person, its heavy chestnut front door shut and its windows warmly lit against a dark evening

storyboard.claim: The house demands complicity to keep up its respectable face.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the handsome timber house presenting a calm front to the street
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from Julia's guilt to the house itself as the thing that demands it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The facade is shown as the lie that the bones sit behind.

storyboard.claim: Time inside Peton is used against the people who live there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a dark title card with the words time and house set against each other
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the complicit people to the way the house itself controls time.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the clock as the next object of attention.

image.subject: a tall antique grandfather clock of dark old wood standing in a dim candlelit living room, its brass pendulum visible through the glass door

storyboard.claim: The grandfather clock is the book's most unsettling object.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the tall clock standing in the candlelit room
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The time theme from the card now has a physical object.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the clock as the house's timekeeper.

image.subject: a close view of an old clock face with brass hands and a heavy brass pendulum blurred in mid-swing behind the glass

storyboard.claim: The pendulum swing is slow and hypnotic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the blurred brass pendulum swinging behind the clock face
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves closer to the clock to show the mechanism in motion.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock is as old as the house, shown through its face.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, sitting bolt upright in an old bed in a dark bedroom, startled awake

storyboard.claim: Julia is woken in the middle of the night by the ticking echo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia sitting up in bed in the dark, startled
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The ticking that filled the first floor has reached her bedroom.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows her awake and alone in the night.

storyboard.claim: A horrific moaning echoes down the second floor hallway.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the sound written out
storyboard.onScreenText: A HORRIFIC MOANING IN THE SECOND FLOOR HALL
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the ticking to a human sound in the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sound is named in words since it has no picture.

image.subject: a bedroom window seen from inside at night, moonlight through the glass, a smudged greasy handprint with unnaturally long thin fingers drying slowly down the outside of the pane

storyboard.claim: Julia finds a long greasy handprint on her window at night.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the smudged handprint with elongated fingers on the outside of the glass
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the moaning, the threat is now on her own window.
storyboard.addedInformation: The print is outside, so someone was on the grounds.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, coming down a staircase in pale morning light, one hand on the banister

storyboard.claim: The next morning Julia goes downstairs and finds something wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia descending the staircase in morning light
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the night at the window to the morning in the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reveal of the stopped clock waits downstairs.

image.subject: a close view of an antique clock face, its two brass hands frozen at 3:41, the heavy pendulum hanging motionless

storyboard.claim: The grandfather clock has stopped at 3:41.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the frozen hands at 3:41 on the clock face
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The clock from the earlier beats has now stopped.
storyboard.addedInformation: The time 3:41 is shown as the key number.

image.subject: a plain old wooden bedroom door in an ordinary house, a small brass lock and a worn key left in it, an everyday ordinary hallway behind

storyboard.claim: A haunting may be ordinary human malice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: an ordinary locked bedroom door with a key in it
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the clock, the narration moves to the explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ordinary door hints that the cause is a person, not a spirit.

storyboard.claim: Strange events make people think of ghosts first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: three short items listed as the strange events
storyboard.onScreenText: A SOUND / A DOOR / A STOPPED CLOCK
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the three events just shown so the viewer can match them.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the idea that the mind reaches for ghosts.

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, standing in a dim doorway half lit by candle

storyboard.claim: A restless ghost is the easier explanation for the mind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a frightened woman in period dress in a candlelit doorway
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The list of events now gets a ghost to match.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ghost is shown as the story the mind wants to believe.

image.subject: a hand resting on the cold iron latch of a heavy dark wooden door inside an old house, a faint candle glow on the wood

storyboard.claim: A living person in the home is orchestrating the fear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a hand on a latch of a door inside the house
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the ghost idea to the living person behind it.
storyboard.addedInformation: A real hand at a real door, not a spirit.

image.subject: a man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, standing in a shadowed candlelit hallway and looking straight ahead

storyboard.claim: Humans are more frightening than ghosts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a stern heavy man in a dark coat in a shadowed hall
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The living person is now given a face.
storyboard.addedInformation: The man is the real threat, not the ghost.

image.subject: a garden rake leaning against a dark wooden living room doorframe, muddy work overalls hanging on a hook beside it, a grandfather clock visible in the room beyond

storyboard.claim: The day after the window, the groundskeeper is in the living room with the clock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a rake against the doorframe and muddy overalls on a hook, no person shown
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The orchestration now has a tool and a place.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rake and overalls point to the groundskeeper without drawing him.

storyboard.claim: The clock stops every night at exactly 3:41 a.m.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the claim written out
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The groundskeeper's claim turns the single stop into a nightly pattern.
storyboard.addedInformation: The nightly repeat is stated in words.

image.subject: an old clock case lying open on a cloth-covered table, its brass gears, springs and iron weights laid out in neat rows beside it

storyboard.claim: A repairman took the whole clock apart and found nothing wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the clock mechanism laid out on cloth in rows
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the claim of the stop to the evidence of the taken-apart clock.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the mechanism that was supposedly inspected.

storyboard.claim: The repairman found nothing wrong with the gears or the weights.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the finding as the punchline
storyboard.onScreenText: NOTHING WRONG. NOTHING WRONG AT ALL.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confirms the repair result as the twist before the watch.
storyboard.addedInformation: The finding is delivered as a bare punchline.

image.subject: a close-up of a silver analog wristwatch lying on a wooden table, its hands frozen at 3:41

storyboard.claim: A wristwatch also stops at 3:41 every night.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the silver watch with hands at 3:41 on a table
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The clock's stop is matched by a second stopped time piece.
storyboard.addedInformation: The second watch makes the stop look like a person's doing.

storyboard.claim: The stopping looks like a supernatural stop of time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the question of ghost or staging
storyboard.onScreenText: A SUPERNATURAL STOP OF TIME, OR A STAGE?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the watch, the question frames the two readings.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the book's reveal as a real choice.

storyboard.claim: 3:41 a.m. may be a historical marker in the family's past.
storyboard.concreteVisual: timeline card with 3:41 a.m. pointing back to a date
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the time into a link to the past.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the stopped time to the 1692 story.

image.subject: a bare field at pale dawn, a charred wooden stake standing in grey ash, a dark timber village far off behind it, no person shown

storyboard.claim: Caroline Eldridge was burned at the stake at 3:41 a.m.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a charred stake in ash in a field at dawn
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The historical time now gets its place, with the violence softened to the aftermath.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stake and ash mark the 1692 death without showing it.

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, standing at a window at dawn with pale light on her face

storyboard.claim: The ghost of Caroline freezes time to make her family face her murder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline at a window at dawn, frightened
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The historical marker now gets a ghost who would stop the clock.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Gothic theory is shown through her face.

storyboard.claim: The ghost theory is pure narrative misdirection.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card naming the theory as misdirection
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the Gothic ghost theory that the previous beat showed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the misdirection as the reason to reject the theory.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, standing in a doorway with one hand over her mouth, shocked

storyboard.claim: Julia believed the ghost story as fully as the viewer did.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia in a doorway, hand over her mouth in shock
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the misdirection is named, Julia's reaction shows she fell for it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her shock marks the moment the story turns against her belief.

image.subject: an elderly woman in her eighties, thin, grey hair in a bun, dark cardigan, stern face, standing in a candlelit hallway in a dark robe, half turned toward the stairs

storyboard.claim: The haunting is a stage play run by the living residents.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ethel in a robe in a candlelit hall, half turned away
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The explanation of the staging now puts a performer on the set.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the performer who is playing Ethel in the house.

image.subject: a low old bedroom with a square trapdoor in the wooden floorboards lifted open onto a dark opening below

storyboard.claim: A hidden trapdoor in a bedroom gives the staging its route.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the square trapdoor lifted open in the bedroom floor
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stage play now has its hidden exit.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the physical route the staging takes through the house.

image.subject: a narrow wooden ladder rising through a dark square hole in a low attic ceiling, old timber beams overhead, a candle on the floor below

storyboard.claim: A seventeenth-century trapdoor leads up through the walls into the attic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a ladder going up through the hole into the dark attic
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The trapdoor from the bedroom now connects to the attic above.
storyboard.addedInformation: The passage through the walls is made visible as a ladder.

storyboard.claim: The narrator asks how the haunting is actually carried out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the logistics question
storyboard.onScreenText: HOW DO THEY FAKE A HAUNTING?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the attic passage, the question asks for the method step by step.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next beats as the answer to the method.

image.subject: a rough hand gripping a heavy brass pendulum to stop it swinging, inside an open clock case in a dim candlelit room

storyboard.claim: The pendulum of the grandfather clock is jammed to stop it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a hand holding the pendulum still inside the clock case
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The method now shows how the clock was stopped.
storyboard.addedInformation: A hand on the pendulum shows the act, not the person.

image.subject: a close-up of a finger pulling out the small crown of a silver wristwatch, the watch lying on a wooden table

storyboard.claim: The wristwatch is stopped by pulling out its crown.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a finger pulling the crown of the silver watch
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The clock method is matched by the watch method.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows how a wristwatch is stopped by hand.

image.subject: a bedroom window seen from the dark garden at night, dewy glass with faint dark streaks running down the pane, no people

storyboard.claim: The living residents move through the hidden halls and drag hands down the windows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: dewy window streaked by downward handprints seen from outside
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the handprint, now seen from outside by the one who made it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows that the saboteurs are outside the glass too.

image.subject: an open old household ledger on a dark wooden table, handwritten columns of names and dates, a candle beside it

storyboard.claim: The haunting aims to scare Julia off so she cannot persuade Letty to sell to the museum.
storyboard.concreteVisual: an open household ledger with handwritten columns beside a candle
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The motive is set out, with the house's own records as the lever.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ledger points to the house's records as the motive for the sale.

storyboard.claim: They gaslight a vulnerable young woman with her family's ghost story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card naming the gaslighting
storyboard.onScreenText: GASLIGHTING A VULNERABLE YOUNG WOMAN WITH HER OWN FAMILY GHOST STORY
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The motive is now named as cruelty toward Julia.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the cruelty into words.

image.subject: the heavy chestnut front door of an old timber house, shut tight, with an iron bear-shaped knocker fixed to the wood

storyboard.claim: Peton's history is used as a weapon to keep physical control of the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the shut front door with the iron bear knocker
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the cruelty to the house itself as the tool.
storyboard.addedInformation: The iron knocker stands for the house as a shield.

image.subject: a row of old framed family portraits on a dark wall, the faces hidden in shadow, a single candle lighting the frames

storyboard.claim: The estate breeds a toxic madness in its inhabitants.
storyboard.concreteVisual: old family portraits with their faces in shadow
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the weapon of history to the people it turns mad.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shadowed family faces show the madness inherited.

storyboard.claim: The inhabitants will do anything, including psychological torture, to keep the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card stating the willingness to do anything
storyboard.onScreenText: THEY WILL DO ANYTHING TO KEEP THE HOUSE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the madness into the price of staying.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the stake of keeping the house in words.

image.subject: a brass house key and a folded old deed lying on a dark wooden table beside a few worn coins

storyboard.claim: The most shocking inheritance in the modern timeline is the theft.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a brass key, a folded deed and worn coins on a table
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the madness to the inheritance that carries it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Key, deed and coins name the inheritance as property.

image.subject: a single flashlight beam cutting through pitch-dark backyard grass, black trees around it and no other light

storyboard.claim: The modern timeline reaches its climax, a mind bender.
storyboard.concreteVisual: one flashlight beam through the black backyard
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The inheritance leads into the yard where the climax happens.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flashlight beam sets the scene for the next beats.
